cohort_total_n_excerpt: Hospital-based 261 prostate cancer cases and 267 controls with benign diseases were recruited from four hospitals in Taiwan.
reason: The case-control component evaluates overall prostate cancer. Stage and Gleason score were compared only among existing prostate cancer cases, so those phenotype analyses do not constitute incident aggressive prostate cancer analyses in an initially cancer-free population.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: High family income, low beef intake, low dairy product consumption and positive family history were independently associated with the prostate carcinogenesis.
estimate_classifications.reason: The beef association concerns overall prostate cancer case status. The abstract's advanced-stage and Gleason analyses are case-only phenotype comparisons and do not make this dietary estimate aggressive.
